# rclone archive extract

Extract archives from source to destination.

## Synopsis



Extract the archive contents to a destination directory auto detecting
the format. See [rclone archive create](/commands/rclone_archive_create/)
for the archive formats supported.

For example on this archive:

```
$ rclonex archive list --long remote:archive.zip
        6 2025-10-30 09:46:23.000000000 file.txt
        0 2025-10-30 09:46:57.000000000 dir/
        4 2025-10-30 09:46:57.000000000 dir/bye.txt
```

You can run extract like this

```
$ rclonex archive extract remote:archive.zip remote:extracted
```

Which gives this result

```
$ rclonex tree remote:extracted
/
├── dir
│   └── bye.txt
└── file.txt
```

The source or destination or both can be local or remote. The source
archive is streamed - it is not downloaded to the local machine first.
Formats which need random access (ZIP, 7z and ISO9660 images) are read
through a sliding window cache of ranged reads; formats which are single
pass (tar, tar.gz ...) are read sequentially. Remotes which do not
support range reads make ZIP, 7z and ISO9660 archives fail with an
explicit error rather than being accessed in some other way. ISO9660
images with Rock Ridge or Joliet extensions are supported, including
their long filenames.

Filters can be used to only extract certain files:

```
$ rclonex archive extract archive.zip partial --include "bye.*"
$ rclonex tree partial
/
└── dir
    └── bye.txt
```

RAR and 7z archives can be encrypted - use --archive-password to set
the password. Multi-volume RAR archives (.part1.rar, .part2.rar, ... or old-style .rar,
.r00, ...) and split 7z archives (.7z.001, .7z.002, ...) are supported and are read
from the source remote volume by volume.

Spanned/multi-disk ZIPs and multi-part TAR archives are not supported.

Memory usage is mostly determined by how much of the archive's metadata
and coding the libraries must hold in memory, not by the size of the
files being extracted:

- ISO9660 images: directories are parsed once as they are walked
  during extraction, so extraction time and memory usage do not depend
  on how many files a single directory holds.
- 7z archives: the whole archive header is parsed before any file is
  extracted, so memory grows with the number of entries - roughly
  140 MiB for 60000 tiny files. The LZMA/LZMA2 dictionary declared by
  the archive is always allocated in full and there is no way to shrink
  it - an archive built with a 128 MiB dictionary needs around that
  much memory again.
- ZIP archives: the central directory is loaded into memory, so memory
  grows with the number of entries - roughly 220 MiB to extract an
  archive holding 200000 files.
- Single-pass formats (tar, tar.gz ...) stream and stay flat regardless
  of the number of files.

`--archive-window-size` only limits the random-access read cache used for
the archive's metadata blocks (16 MiB by default; 0 disables caching).
It does not limit the dictionary or metadata memory described above.

The [archive backend](/archive/) can also be used to extract files. It
can be used to read only mount archives also but it supports a
different set of archive formats to the archive commands.


```
rclonex archive extract [flags] <source> <destination>
```

## Options

```
      --archive-continue-on-error   Continue on errors instead of aborting extraction
      --archive-password string     Password for encrypted RAR and 7z archives
      --archive-window-size int     Sliding window cache size in bytes for random-access archives (ZIP, 7z, ISO9660); 0 disables caching (default 16777216)
  -h, --help                       help for extract
```

See the [global flags page](/flags/) for global options not listed here.
